title: Sara Duterte to form legal, IT teams to guard against 2028 poll cheating
summary: MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte on Friday shared that her camp started preparing her legal and information technology (IT) teams for her campaign in the 2028 elections for possible…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte on Friday shared that her camp started preparing her legal and information technology (IT) teams for her campaign in the 2028 elections for possible election cheating occurrences.
This is what Duterte answered when she was asked of her preparations for the much-anticipated elections after she declared her presidential bid as early as February this year.
“We’re not prepared on the ground. What we prepared is the legal team because this will be a fight against cheating in the elections,” Duterte said in a press conference.
Duterte also said that they already talked to election lawyers and some of them committed to joining her legal team.
“The next thing that we are preparing for is the IT team because this will be, as I said, fight against election cheating, particularly the automations,” she added.
Duterte then shared that the network on the ground is “very stable” from 2016 or since her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte assumed presidency and up to the 2019 and 2025 midterm elections.

Meanwhile, Duterte said that the administration might push for charter change, or the amendment of the 1987 Constitution, noting that many public officials were raising the possibility of it throughout the years.

She noted that the “no el” or no elections scenario will only happen through the amendment of the Constitution. She added that there were two lawmakers from the House of Representatives who were allegedly hatching plans for charter change, though she did not name them.
Senior Deputy Speaker Ferdinand Hernandez last Thursday debunked the claims that members of the House of Representatives are forming plans to postpone the 2028 elections.

Last Sunday, Commission on Elections (Comelec) Chairperson George Erwin Garcia once again dismissed the claims of the “no el” scenario in 2028 as he emphasized that the poll body is currently preparing for the elections.

Garcia noted that the poll body will allocate P22 billion to lease automated counting machines (ACMs) for the elections. He said that they will begin the bidding process for the internet voting system and transmission services and that the procurement process for the ACMs will start by December this year.

Last June, Garcia also said that a “no el” scenario in 2028 through an amendment of the Constitution is not possible due to the lack of rules allowing it. He noted that the rule to amend the Constitution is suspended.

In January 2024, the Comelec suspended any proceedings regarding people’s initiative to amend the 1987 Constitution. The Comelec Resolution No. 10650, promulgated in January 2020, served as the implementing rules and regulations of Republic Act No. 6735, or the Initiative and Referendum Act.

Under the said resolution, any registered voter or group of voters may file a petition for an initiative or referendum to “propose, enact, approve or reject, in whole or in part, the Constitution, laws, ordinances or resolutions passed by any legislative body.” /jpv
